chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ubayhi, from Ubayd ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Sustenance is assigned to foolishness, and deprivation is assigned to intellect, and affliction is assigned to patience.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between intellect, foolishness, and sustenance in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine wisdom behind the distribution of sustenance (rizq), deprivation (hirmān), and trials (bala'), linking them respectively to simplicity (humq), intellect ('aql), and patience (sabr). Shia scholars often interpret 'humq' not as mere foolishness but as a state of humble reliance on God that invites provision, whereas 'aql' may denote calculated self-sufficiency that leads to spiritual deprivation. This triad underscores the Shia emphasis on inner disposition and divine decree over mere worldly calculation.

en.hubeali: H 14725 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ubeyd Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn, from Ali Bin Al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather who said:
Amir-ul-Momineenasws said: ‘The sustenance is allocated to the foolishness, and the deprivation to the intellect, and the affliction to the patience’.
